description: I am a full-stack web developer who is fluent in Typescript, HTML, CSS, Python, and C++. I am interested in solving real-world problems and creating solutions using software.
summary: Many people in the world have visual impairment and are unable to see the data given from NASA’s visuals. I solved this issue by creating Sonora, a web application that scans surface temperature data from NASA’s Goddard Earth Observing System (GEOS) and plays a pitch based on the temperature in each longitude.
details:
The app is meant for people with vision impairment by helping them understand the world through audio instead of sight.

My app allows its users to get an auditory representation of surface temperature data by scanning latitude by latitude and play 128 different frequencies based on each latitude's temperature. Colder temperatures produce lower frequencies (minimum of -35°C and 20 Hz) and warmer temperatures produce higher pitches (maximum of 35°C and 5 kHz). It also pans each frequency based on its longitude from the center of the map.

It uses NASA's GEOS-5 FP forecast through the NCCS OPeNDAP endpoint to load the hourly global surface temperature at 2 meters and also draws it onto a canvas that is color scaled using Turbo.

It also provides spoken instructions and narrates user interaction through Speech Synthesis API and the user can search a location using the Mapbox Geocoding API and hear the temperature data of that area.

This app was coded using Typescript, HTML, CSS, and Python and uses Vite to build the frontend and Flask to run the backend API.
